name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,150

indicators.note: handled in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written; the possessive is only a joining 'is'

explanation.surface: A cleric's party line has been received in an odd, unorthodox way.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. Six letters of the clergyman rearrange into a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a narrow band of colour, so it can be called a line drawn across a surface.

clue.text: Give strength to us in disgrace

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a stain on one's name is a disgrace

explanation.surface: Someone asks for support to get through a shameful episode.
explanation.walkthrough: The small pronoun sits inside the word for a blot on one's reputation, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain someone is to keep them going, supporting them physically or morally through hardship.

clue.text: France, say, removing pub, a survival from the past

indicators.note: taking something away means those letters are cut out of the longer word

blocks.note: France is an example of a republic
taken as written

explanation.surface: France getting rid of its bars would be losing a historic institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France, say' is a definition by example: France is one kind of republic. Lift the bar out of the middle and what is left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object or custom that has lasted on from an earlier era, exactly a survival of old times.

clue.text: Sort out beforehand perimeter being confused with end

indicators.note: things that are confused are muddled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Planning ahead, someone muddles up the boundary of a field with where it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the boundary word and the short word for a finish go into the mix; 'with' simply adds the second to the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To predetermine something is to settle or decide it in advance, before events unfold.

blocks.note: first meaning: move past something
second meaning: a way through a gap between peaks

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to travel over the hills; really the two phrases are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for moving past and a noun for a gap through a mountain range used as a road.

blocks.note: taken as written
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone wants to cut a match short.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is the card game for four players in partnerships, placed after the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book or speech is to cut it down in length while keeping its substance.

indicators.note: something spoken is heard rather than read, so we go by how a word sounds

blocks.note: seen means observed, and has the same sound as a division of a drama

explanation.surface: A spoken section of a stage drama has been watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoken part of play' looks like a phrase for dialogue, but 'spoken' belongs to the wordplay and only 'part of play' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is one of the divisions of an act in a stage play, set in a single place.

blocks.note: first meaning: a prop or brace, such as a rope steadying a mast
second meaning: not leave

explanation.surface: It reads like a political slogan backing one side of a referendum on leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes 'Support Remain' look like a campaign slogan from the Brexit vote; in fact each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a brace or prop holding something up; as a verb it means continue in place.

clue.text: See grub here cooked to follow cold fast food

indicators.note: food that is cooked is transformed, so the letters are worked into a new form
following means coming after, which fixes the order of the two parts

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner invites us to watch food being cooked to go with a cold dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words at the start are all fodder; the reworked letters come after the cold-tap abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseburger is a hamburger topped with melted cheese, a staple item at quick-service restaurants.

blocks.note: first meaning: able to pay one's debts
second meaning: a liquid that dissolves grease or dirt

explanation.surface: Someone with cash is looking to hire domestic help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' suggests a person who cleans houses, but here it is a chemical that dissolves dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvent describes a business or person able to meet debts, and also names a dissolving liquid such as white spirit.

indicators.note: wearing something means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
hose is an old word for stockings or tights

explanation.surface: It asks whether an Arab man is going about in women's hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab perhaps' points at a person, but Arab is also a breed of horse, so this is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian, often shortened to Arab, is a famous breed of horse prized for speed and endurance.

indicators.note: in a strange manner means oddly arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A preacher's sermon is odd, yet surprisingly fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' looks like an adjective praising the preaching, but it is a noun: the first model from which copies come.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern or prototype on which later versions are modelled.

indicators.note: to kill something is to get rid of it, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: a duke is the highest rank of British nobleman
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A distinguished aristocrat has murdered the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' seems to praise the nobleman, but it means unpaid, as a bill still owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still unpaid, and a payment that is due is one owed now.

indicators.note: adding something on puts it at the end, which sets the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a fruitcake is slang for an eccentric person, as is a nut
Meg is a short form of Margaret, as is Maggie

explanation.surface: A baker named Maggie puts spice into a fruitcake mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' suggests baking, but it is informal for a crazy person; one nickname for Margaret swaps for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, grated as a spice into cakes and puddings.

blocks.note: a tin is a can
to foil a plan is to frustrate it

explanation.surface: Cooking equipment can be a source of annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a modal verb but is the noun container; 'frustrate' is a verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheet used in kitchens to wrap food or line baking trays.

blocks.note: first meaning: a traditional story
second meaning: a very famous person

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a tabloid phrase about a star's invented image; the two nouns are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a traditional tale, and also a hugely famous figure, as in 'a screen great' or living icon.

clue.text: Sleeping porter missing his third shift finally

indicators.note: lacking a numbered letter of its own word means that single letter is taken out
the final position of a word is its closing letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: a doorman is a porter at a building's entrance
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A doorkeeper is asleep on the job and misses the third shift of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His third' refers back to the porter word: take out its third letter, an O. 'Third shift' looks like a phrase but splits across two devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or at rest, like an animal hibernating or a volcano not erupting.

blocks.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
something surrounded is in, enclosed

explanation.surface: A pawn is hemmed in during a chess attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies a short word for enclosed, placed after the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a pin is a tactic where an attacked piece cannot move without exposing a more valuable one behind it.

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: Someone goes silent in annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall quiet' reads as one phrase meaning hush, but 'Fall' alone is the definition and 'quiet' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch is to plunge or topple forward, as when someone is thrown headlong from a horse.

clue.text: When days are longer minute by minute perhaps?

definitions.text: When days are longer minute by minute perhaps?

blocks.note: surface reading: the season of long daylight
setter's reading: daylight grows by a few minutes each day as the year climbs to its peak

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the season by the way daylight stretches a little each day until the solstice; the question mark flags the loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer is the period around the June solstice, when daylight hours reach their longest of the year.

clue.text: Concealed five hundred on Noah’s ship

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the ark is the vessel Noah built for the flood

explanation.surface: Five hundred stowaways were hidden aboard Noah's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numeral sits on top of the vessel because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something dark is to keep it secret, so the word can mean hidden from knowledge.

clue.text: Second time I note recurring image

blocks.note: a mo is a short moment, a second
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
F is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A second time, someone notices an image that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recurring' seems to signal a reversal, but it belongs to the definition; the pieces read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a distinctive theme or pattern repeated through a work of art, music or literature.

clue.text: Ripped, pierced by hard, sharp object

indicators.note: something pierced has another thing driven into it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: torn means ripped
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Fabric was torn when something hard and pointed went through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'hard' hides that 'sharp object' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a stiff pointed spike on a plant stem, a natural sharp point that can prick skin.

clue.text: Revised a target for rowing competition

indicators.note: something revised is reworked and changed, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crew coach has set a new goal for the boat race.
explanation.walkthrough: The article joins the fodder: all seven letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting event made up of a series of boat races, usually rowing or sailing.

clue.text: About to leave icy high ground

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so that letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: chill as an adjective means icy cold
c (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to set off from frozen uplands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to leave' reads as 'on the point of departing', but 'About' is the Latin-derived abbreviation and 'to leave' the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill is a naturally raised area of land, lower than a mountain, so it is elevated terrain.

definitions.note: plural noun defining a mass noun

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone backs earnings that are appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin preposition supplies the opening chunk, then a short adjective for proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is the financial gain left over after costs, so it covers money earned.
